subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should raw `openclaw.json` env provider keys be supported as durable managed-Gateway runtime auth, or should daemon users be steered to `.env`, SecretRef, or per-agent auth profiles instead?
rationale: The source path is clear enough to show an auth/status mismatch risk, but the repair changes credential materialization and diagnostic semantics across config, daemon install, and provider auth surfaces.

options.title: Support config env for Gateway runtime
options.body: Keep documented `env.KIMI_API_KEY` support and add the service-env/status/docs/tests needed to make managed Gateway turns and diagnostics agree without unnecessarily exposing raw secrets.

options.title: Make daemon auth use `.env` or profiles
options.body: Treat raw config env as non-durable CLI/config input and update Kimi docs plus `models status` wording/JSON so daemon users are guided to `.env`, SecretRef, or per-agent auth profiles.

options.title: Add warning-only guard first
options.body: Add a doctor/status/startup warning for managed keys that are declared but not resolvable, then defer the durable credential contract choice.

recommendation.title: Support config env for Gateway runtime
recommendation.body: Keep documented `env.KIMI_API_KEY` support and add the service-env/status/docs/tests needed to make managed Gateway turns and diagnostics agree without unnecessarily exposing raw secrets.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans config IO and service-env planning, which are the contract surfaces needing a decision.
